SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close shuts down the pool. Arroyo can close a strategy on partition revocation/rebalance and later create a new strategy from the same factory. After the first close, the pool's queues and worker threads are permanently shut down, so later submissions will fail and be treated as completed, allowing unprocessed messages to be committed."

      "body": "FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True before draining queues, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join/close never waits for wait_until_empty. Workers therefore stop after their current item, leaving queued WorkItems unprocessed. OrderedQueueWorker also never calls work_queue.task_done(), so any shutdown/join path that depends on unfinished tasks cannot complete correctly. On consumer shutdown, queued messages can be discarded and completed offsets may not be committed."

This can raise RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration. The commit loop catches the exception, but that iteration's commits are skipped, which can delay offset commits during partition churn."

This can exhaust memory; the claimed 'natural backpressure' does not exist."

The CLI option should validate that max_workers is positive."

findings.title: Uses Python 3.13-only queue shutdown APIs
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker catches queue.ShutDown (also at line 142) and FixedQueuePool.shutdown calls Queue.shutdown(immediate=False) at line 238. queue.ShutDown and Queue.shutdown were added in Python 3.13. If this consumer runs on an older Python interpreter supported by Sentry, attribute resolution or the shutdown call will fail at runtime, breaking worker exception handling and/or graceful shutdown. This needs a compatibility fallback or an explicit Python 3.13+ requirement.

findings.title: Strategy.close shuts down a shared queue pool that may be reused after rebalance
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool per factory (result_consumer.py line 133) and passes that same pool to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy (result_consumer.py line 254). SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close shuts down the pool. Arroyo can close a strategy on partition revocation/rebalance and later create a new strategy from the same factory. After the first close, the pool's queues and worker threads are permanently shut down, so later submissions will fail and be treated as completed, allowing unprocessed messages to be committed.

findings.title: Shutdown does not drain queues and can drop pending work
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True before draining queues, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join/close never waits for wait_until_empty. Workers therefore stop after their current item, leaving queued WorkItems unprocessed. OrderedQueueWorker also never calls work_queue.task_done(), so any shutdown/join path that depends on unfinished tasks cannot complete correctly. On consumer shutdown, queued messages can be discarded and completed offsets may not be committed.

findings.title: OffsetTracker iterates all_offsets keys while other threads mutate it
findings.body: get_committable_offsets builds list(self.all_offsets.keys()) without a global lock while submit()/add_offset() can concurrently insert new Partition keys. This can raise RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration. The commit loop catches the exception, but that iteration's commits are skipped, which can delay offset commits during partition churn.

findings.title: Work queues are unbounded, providing no backpressure
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() uses put() unconditionally. If workers are slower than incoming Kafka messages (for example due to a slow subscription), the consumer will continue polling and queueing decoded WorkItems without bound, retaining both decoded results and original messages. This can exhaust memory; the claimed 'natural backpressure' does not exist.

findings.title: Offsets are completed even when processing fails
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in a finally block even when result_processor raises. ResultProcessor.__call__ also swallows handling exceptions. Therefore a message that fails handling (for example a transient DB error) is treated as done and becomes committable. The consumer will commit past it and never retry it, despite the strategy's documentation saying offsets are committed only after successful processing.

findings.title: submit() marks failed submissions as completed, allowing unprocessed offsets to commit
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit catches all exceptions and, when broker metadata is present, adds and immediately completes the offset. If queue_pool.submit fails (for example because the queue is shut down, the pool is in a bad state, or an unexpected error occurs before enqueue), the message is never processed but is still considered complete, so the commit loop may commit it and silently lose the result.

findings.title: Committable-offset calculation scans integer ranges and sets repeatedly
findings.body: Every commit-loop iteration computes min(all_offsets) and max(all_offsets) for each partition and then loops over every integer from start to max_offset. With large batches, many outstanding offsets, or a stuck offset, this can become CPU-intensive. The per-partition offset sets also grow until a contiguous prefix can be committed, increasing memory pressure during backlogs.

findings.title: join() ignores its timeout and does not flush pending work
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join(timeout) simply calls close(), which stops the commit thread with a fixed 5-second join and shuts down the pool without waiting for queued items or honoring the supplied timeout. Arroyo's join contract is to allow pending processing to finish up to the timeout; this implementation can terminate early and leave work unprocessed/uncommitted.

findings.title: Hash-distribution test is nondeterministic
findings.body: test_different_groups_distributed asserts that 20 hashed group names hit all three queues. Python's randomized string hashing does not guarantee that every bucket is hit for this small sample, so the test can fail intermittently. It should use a deterministic hash function or only assert consistent assignment.

findings.title: Negative --max-workers creates an invalid queue pool
findings.body: For thread-queue-parallel mode, num_queues is set to max_workers or 20. A negative max_workers value is truthy, so FixedQueuePool receives a negative num_queues; range(num_queues) creates no queues and hash(group_key) % negative_num_queues can produce invalid indices. The CLI option should validate that max_workers is positive.
